message.content:
It looks like you’re mixing up two different “start” commands:

| What you’re probably trying to do | Command you’d normally use |
|-----------------------------------|----------------------------|
| **Start the Docker *service* (so you can run `docker` commands)** | `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (PowerShell) or `net start com.docker.service` (cmd) |
| **Start a *container* that’s already been created** | `docker start <container‑name-or‑ID>` |

---

### 1️⃣ Starting the Docker Service (Windows)

If you just want Docker Desktop (or the Docker Engine) to be running so you can issue `docker` commands, you can start the service from a PowerShell prompt:

```powershell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

Or from the classic command prompt:

```cmd
net start com.docker.service
```

> **Tip:**  
> • Make sure Docker Desktop is installed and that the `com.docker.service` service exists.  
> • If you’re using Docker Desktop, you can also simply launch the Docker Desktop GUI – it will automatically start the background service.

---

### 2️⃣ Starting an Existing Container

If you already have a container that you stopped and now want to bring back up, you’ll need its name or ID:

```bash
docker start my_container
```

Replace `my_container` with the actual container name or ID.  
If you’re not sure what containers exist, list them first:

```bash
docker ps -a
```

---

#### Quick Summary

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Start Docker Desktop / Engine | `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` (PowerShell) or `net start com.docker.service` (cmd) |
| Start a stopped container | `docker start <container-name-or-ID>` |

Let me know which one you’re after, or if you need help with anything else!
